annotator_prompt.name: lifted_count
annotator_prompt.description: Replace this field with completed_targets below. After highlighted cubes were lifted and returned, the color-and-position prefix definition failed to count genuine completed pickups. It consequently left already handled targets eligible and sometimes remained at zero after a completed lift. This breaks SUFFICIENCY and PREDICTABILITY. The recorded executions do not follow the prescribed red–green–blue, increasing-y order. A scalar prefix count cannot represent their progress without an independently justified target order.

annotator_prompt.name: completed_targets
annotator_prompt.description: The goal requires picking up each individually highlighted cube, but after a cube is returned its completed pickup is no longer visible. Replace the prefix count with the identities of highlighted cubes whose completed lifts have been observed, independent of pickup order. Assign stable identifiers to the highlighted cubes in highlight_frame by increasing world y, then increasing world x, numbered starting at 1; this numbering identifies cubes and does not prescribe pickup order. Store completed identifiers as a sorted list serialized as text, initially "[]". Add an identifier at the first cycle showing that cube held off the table with TCP approximately z=0.15 after a pickup lift. Never add it at the grasp or when the lift is merely commanded. Preserve membership after release, return, and retreat, and never add an identity twice. Example: "[1, 3]". Annotate every actual completed highlighted pickup, including those previously excluded by the erroneous prefix rule. This repairs the historical-progress component of SUFFICIENCY and PREDICTABILITY without retaining a redundant count.

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: lifted_count
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: Remove this field and its fixed-order prefix interpretation; use completed_targets instead. The previous instruction excluded visibly completed pickups solely because their identities were not next in an unsupported ordering. This made memory updates and later target selection inconsistent with the execution.

policy_prompt_for_memory.name: completed_targets
policy_prompt_for_memory.description: After highlighted cubes have been returned, the present scene cannot establish which were previously lifted, so preserve completed identities rather than an ordered-prefix count. From highlight_frame, number only the individually highlighted cubes by increasing world y, then increasing world x, starting at 1. These are stable identity labels, not pickup priorities. Initialize the text value to "[]". Match a held cube to its original highlighted identity using position, color, and this cycle's motion frames. When this cycle visibly shows a completed pickup lift of that identity, held off the table with TCP approximately z=0.15, add its identifier and serialize the identifiers in increasing numeric order, for example "[1, 3]". Add any newly completed highlighted identity regardless of selection order. Preserve the set through release and retreat. Do not add identities for low grasps, commanded lifts, empty grasps, or an action executing no steps. Membership prevents double counting a previously lifted cube still being held. This makes updates recognizable from the available observations and repairs PREDICTABILITY.

proposal.policy_prompt_for_action: When the highlights disappeared and the hand was ready to leave the button, the prescribed color-and-position order selected a different cube from the recorded approach. The same rule then redirected an already aligned hand away from its recorded grasp target. After returns, erroneous prefix counts also caused previously lifted cubes to be selected again. These are SUFFICIENCY failures, not failures to retain the highlight display. Remove every red–green–blue pickup-priority rule, every increasing-y pickup-priority rule, and every interpretation of progress as an ordered prefix. Use completed_targets to exclude completed identities; its geometric numbering is only an identity convention. Recognize a newly completed lift from current observations before deciding whether additional targets remain. Return a held completed cube at the current TCP x,y to z=0.01 and open when an uncompleted highlighted target remains; retain the existing open-hand vertical retreat before lateral travel. Keep the final highlighted cube held. An open hand already hovering within the existing alignment tolerance above an uncompleted highlighted cube should descend to that cube at z=0.02 and close, rather than redirecting because of color priority. Preserve the calibrated edge-aligned orientation and existing lift rules. There is still an unresolved selection ambiguity when several uncompleted highlighted cubes are available and the hand is not already aligned over one: the supplied goal gives no order, and the complete executions contradict the previous ordering without establishing a replacement observable ordering rule. Do not invent episode-specific exceptions or encode future recorded actions into memory. Matching the recorded free-choice approach waypoints requires an independently supplied, runtime-observable selection rule, or an evaluation that accepts alternative valid target orders. Separately, a correctly selected cube was localized more than 1 cm away because its top-face plane was left unspecified. Specify a resting-cube top-face plane approximately 0.04 m above the tabletop for the cubes shown here, rather than leaving the surface height unconstrained. Back-project the top-face center onto that plane with the appropriate calibrated camera, refine with the current wrist view when available, and retain the separately specified TCP hover and grasp heights. Do not project a top-face center onto the tabletop or treat the grasp TCP height as the cube's top height.
proposal.refused: Do not pass on the proposed rule that an out-of-order highlighted lift must remain uncounted. That proposal follows the defective prefix convention, whereas the goal requires all highlighted cubes to be picked up and the full executions visibly complete those lifts. Likewise, reports describing a later pickup as the first pickup, or claiming that a blue cube should follow only one completed red pickup, relied on stale counts: the complete executions show two distinct completed pickups before those later approaches. Their progress should be repaired, not used to infer additional priority exceptions. One report also called the approached blue cube green and reversed the identity associated with its proposed coordinates; its identity-specific correction contradicts the images and is excluded. The reports correctly establish that the old ordering is wrong, but they do not establish a general replacement order. No color, spatial, or episode-specific priority is asserted without evidence.

Retain that label thereafter, including after the highlights disappear. The white square supporting the button is not a cube highlight. e.g. "E17"

fields.name: button_pressed
fields.description: Initialize false. Set true when this cycle shows the closed fingertips down in contact with the button following a pressing descent, including a contact-limited TCP height around z=0.024. Otherwise preserve the carried value. Highlights alone do not establish a press. e.g. false

fields.name: completed_targets
fields.description: Initialize to "[]". From highlight_frame, number only the individually highlighted cubes by increasing original world y, then increasing original world x, starting at 1. These are stable identity labels, not pickup priorities; never renumber using positions changed by handling. Match a held cube to its highlighted identity using position, color, and this cycle's motion frames. Add its identifier when this cycle visibly shows it held off the table after a completed pickup lift with TCP approximately z=0.15, regardless of selection order. Serialize the identifiers in increasing numeric order with a comma and space between entries. Preserve membership through lowering, release, and retreat. Do not add identities for low grasps, commanded lifts, empty grasps, or an action executing no steps. An identity already present must not be added again when its cube remains held. e.g. "[1, 3]"

texts.action:
Start with an open hand and approach the button. Interpret all positions in world coordinates using the supplied camera calibration; estimate button and cube locations from their geometry, not raw image left/right. Back-project a visible surface center onto that surface's horizontal height plane, not automatically onto z=0. Estimate surface height and center from object geometry and both calibrated current views where available. For pixel p=(u,v,1), use the corresponding camera's calibration to compute world ray origin C=-R^T t and direction d=R^T K^-1 p. Intersect with the surface plane z=h using X=C+((h-C_z)/d_z)d. Use the current wrist camera's extrinsics for wrist pixels, not the front camera's extrinsics. For the button, localize the raised circular pressing surface rather than its white base. For a resting cube, localize the top-face center, not the center of the entire visible silhouette. For the approximately 4 cm cubes, use a top-face plane approximately 0.04 m above the tabletop, refining the height from visible cube geometry and calibrated views. Back-project the top-face center onto that plane using the appropriate camera calibration and refine with the current calibrated wrist view. Neither the tabletop plane nor the prescribed grasp TCP height is the cube's top-face plane. Use the resulting world x,y for object-centered approach and contact waypoints, retaining the separately specified TCP waypoint heights. Use the wrist view to refine alignment. Approximate hover alignment permits the next operation but does not make the achieved TCP x,y the object center. Recover target identities from highlight_frame after their white areas disappear, matching by position as well as color; never select every cube of a highlighted color. Use the observations of this cycle together with carried memory to recognize newly completed presses and lifts before selecting the action.

Button rules: If button_pressed is false and the hand is not yet above the button, move to its center at z=0.15, roll=-3.1416, pitch=0, yaw=0, gripper open. At approximate button hover, allow normal approach error of roughly 1–1.5 cm to proceed to the next operation, but do not treat the achieved TCP x,y as the button center. Before closing and again before pressing, estimate the button center from the current calibrated views, refining it with the wrist image. With open fingers at approximate hover, command that button-centered x,y at z=0.15 and close on arrival. With closed fingers at approximate hover and no observed contact yet, descend directly to the newly estimated button-centered x,y at z=0.0075 with fingers closed. Once contact is observed, retract to the button center at z=0.15, keeping closed; do not repeat the press merely because the actual contact height is higher than the command. After retracting, open at the button approach waypoint before traveling to a cube.

Pickup rules: Recover individually highlighted identities from highlight_frame using the same stable numbering as completed_targets. Robot-right is negative y and appears on the left of the front image. Match identities by position as well as color; numbering is not pickup priority. Exclude every identity in completed_targets, including any newly completed lift observed this cycle. If the open hand at hover is already aligned within roughly 1–1.5 cm above an uncompleted highlighted cube, select that cube and descend rather than redirecting to another target. Otherwise, when ready for lateral travel, select an uncompleted highlighted cube; absent an explicit goal ordering, any such target is eligible. Do not infer a color or spatial pickup priority from the identity numbering. With open fingers and adequate table clearance, approach its center at z=0.15. Use roll=3.1416 and pitch=0. Back-project two endpoints of a cube top-face edge onto the same top-face height plane using the calibrated ray-plane intersection. From their world-coordinate difference compute theta=atan2(delta_y,delta_x). Choose among theta+k*pi/2, for integer k, the square-equivalent edge-aligned yaw requiring the least angular rotation from the current hand yaw, accounting for angle wrapping. Do not negate theta based on image appearance or copy an image-plane edge angle. Preserve that alignment during descent and lift. Only when the open hand is approximately aligned above the selected uncompleted target, descend to its center at z=0.02 and close. Allow normal approach error of roughly 1–1.5 cm; if already aligned, descend rather than commanding another hover. An open hand at hover above a returned, completed cube must instead approach an uncompleted highlighted target at z=0.15 with fingers open. With the cube grasped at low height, lift vertically to z=0.15 with fingers closed, preserving the aligned yaw. Estimate its grasp center from the visible cube and wrist geometry rather than treating a small TCP tracking error as a new target location.

Handling additional targets: Once a pickup lift is visibly complete, include its identity in completed_targets even if the cube is subsequently returned. Recognize this completion before deciding whether any uncompleted highlighted target remains. If one remains and a completed cube is still held at hover height, lower at the current TCP x,y to z=0.01, retaining current orientation, and open on arrival. If the hand is low and open over that returned cube, retract vertically to approximately z=0.15 with fingers open before moving laterally. When retracted, approach an uncompleted highlighted target, not the cube just returned. When every highlighted identity is completed, keep the final lifted cube held; success should end the episode without requiring a placement.

For every gripper-only change, first construct the nominal object-centered waypoint rather than copying the achieved TCP pose. If that waypoint already provides at least 2 mm of translation from the reported TCP pose, do not add a nudge. Otherwise add a small upward adjustment within 5 mm so that the translation is at least 2 mm. Do not advance memory on an action that executed no steps. If alignment or grasp evidence is ambiguous, use the current wrist image to correct the relevant object-centered approach at safe height; a failed empty grasp should be retried without counting it. If no target evidence has yet been captured after the button operation, use a short bounded wait specifically to observe the highlight display and inspect every returned frame. Do not invent targets or repeatedly press a confirmed button. For an otherwise unmatched situation, preserve known task facts, keep a visibly held cube closed, and retract vertically to safe clearance before reassessing.

applied.refused: The Round 1 fixed-order prefix correction is replaced, rather than reversed into another universal ordering. Across Rounds 2–4, observed completed pickups contradict both its color priority and its same-color priority; this round establishes that these restrictions also suppress genuine memory updates. Stable completed identities preserve actual progress without choosing among the mutually conflicting orders. No replacement color or spatial priority, episode-specific exception, future-action memory, or color relabeling is committed. Free-choice approach waypoints remain underdetermined when several eligible targets exist and the hand is not aligned over one: allowing a valid target does not claim to reproduce the recorded choice. Exact matching there still requires an independently observable selection rule or evaluation accepting alternative valid orders. The approximately 0.04 m cube height is committed as a geometry-dependent estimate, not an unconditional world-z constant. Earlier calibrated localization, object-centered button operation, translation safeguard, and return-and-retreat corrections are retained.
